newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Lion Nathan dispels takeover talk.
newsitem.headline: Lion Nathan dispels takeover talk.

text.p: Lion Nathan Ltd Director of Corporate Affairs Graham Seatter said on Thursday the company was unaware of any possible takeover, rumours of which have persisted in the market since the New Year.
"They are just rumours," Seatter told Reuters.
Shares in the brewing and beverage company were within striking distance of 12-month highs in early Thursday trade as takeover rumours refused to go away.
Lion, which has risen sharply over the last few days, initially added another six cents to trade at NZ$3.85, 10 cents short of a 12 month high. The stock later eased to NZ$3.78.
Brokers were in the dark as to whether the talk had any validity, although they pointed out Lion had attracted high turnover in recent weeks.
"It's pretty hard to explain movements in share prices," Seatter said.
On January 10, Lion Chief Executive Douglas Myers dispelled rumours that he had been approached by parties for his 16 percent stake.

"I think Douglas answered the speculation, or the comment, that came out of Australia with respect to his shares being on the block and that remains the position. There is no change to that," Seatter said.

"In terms of explaining the share price movement, I guess the only thing we can really say is that most international analyses of beer stocks suggest that our shares are very much undervalued compared to other stocks," he said.
Lion was under downward pressure last year as the market became concerned about management changes and slippage in its Australian market share.

"Maybe that is correcting and maybe some of the speculation with respect to management changes and market share et cetera had something of an over-reaction which is now disappearing," Seatter said. "There is nothing that we are aware of beyond that." -- Wellington Newsroom (64-4-4734746)
